report:
### Conclusion
Your sister’s view is supported by clinical evidence. Preoperative skin preparation with chlorhexidine–alcohol significantly reduces the risk of surgical-site infections (SSI) following cesarean delivery compared to iodine–alcohol solutions.

### Key Evidence
1. **Landmark Randomized Controlled Trial**: A definitive study published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* (Tuuli et al., 2016) involving 1,147 patients found that chlorhexidine–alcohol skin antisepsis reduced the rate of post-cesarean SSI by over 40% compared to iodine–alcohol (4.0% vs. 7.3%) ([NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1511048)).
2. **Cochrane Systematic Review**: A 2020 Cochrane review analyzed multiple randomized clinical trials and concluded with moderate certainty that chlorhexidine gluconate is more effective at preventing post-cesarean wound infections than povidone-iodine preparations ([Cochrane Library](https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD007462.pub5/full)).
3. **Clinical Guidance**: Professional medical bodies, including the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), recognize alcohol-based chlorhexidine as an effective skin preparation choice for abdominal surgery due to its rapid bactericidal activity and persistent efficacy ([The ObG Project](https://www.obgproject.com/2018/09/30/chlorhexidine-or-iodine-based-skin-prep-for-cesarean-sections/)).

Chlorhexidine–alcohol is widely considered the superior skin antiseptic for preventing surgical-site infections during cesarean deliveries.
